Rashi on Niddah 43b:10:1.hebrew: שתים וקראו טמא - כי יהיה זב מבשרו - חדא, זובו טמא - תרי, טמא:
Rashi on Niddah 43b:10:1.english: Two and called him impure - "When [any man] has an emission out of his flesh" is one; "his emission is impure" is two; [and the verse called him] "impure."

Rashi on Niddah 43b:10:2.hebrew: שלש וקראו טמא - זאת תהיה טומאתו בזובו - חדא, רר בשרו את זובו - תרי, או החתים בשרו מזובו - תלת; טומאתו היא:
Rashi on Niddah 43b:10:2.english: Three and called him impure - "This shall be his impurity in his emission" is one; "his flesh runs with his emission" is two; "or his flesh is stopped from his emission" is three; [and] "it is his impurity" [is where it called him impure].

Rashi on Niddah 43b:12:1.english: Concerning the discharge - That the drop itself is impure.

Rashi on Niddah 43b:13:1.hebrew: לנוגע בכעדשה - דמנגיעה דשרץ נפקא לן נגיעה דש"ז לקמן, מאו איש אשר יגע וגו':
Rashi on Niddah 43b:13:1.english: To one who touches, in a lentil-bulk - For from contact with a creeping animal we derive contact with semen later, from: "Or a man who touches," etc.

Rashi on Niddah 43b:14:1.hebrew: אין לו חלוקת טומאה - דשרץ קטן מטמא כגדול, אבל קטן פחות מבן ט' אין לו קרי:
Rashi on Niddah 43b:14:1.english: There is no differentiation in its impurity - For a small creeping animal imparts impurity like a large one, but a minor younger than nine years old has no [halakhic status of] seminal emission.

Rashi on Niddah 43b:16:1.hebrew: שום שרץ קתני - אין לך שרץ מטמא במשהו, אבל ש"ז יש מטמא במשהו, כגון לרואה:
Rashi on Niddah 43b:16:1.english: It teaches the category of a creeping animal - There is no creeping animal that imparts impurity in any amount, but [regarding] semen, there is [that which] imparts impurity in any amount, such as for one who emits [it].

Rashi on Niddah 43b:18:1.hebrew: דכוליה במקום כעדשה קאי - כלומר, מתוך חשיבותיה שהוא אבר, הוי חשוב במקום כעדשה:
Rashi on Niddah 43b:18:1.english: For all of it stands in place of a lentil-bulk - That is to say, due to its significance in that it is a limb, it is considered in place of a lentil-bulk.

Rashi on Niddah 43b:18:2.hebrew: תדע דמשום חשיבותא דאבר הוא, דהא אילו חסר פורתא - מן האבר, דהוי בציר מכעדשה, מי מטמא:
Rashi on Niddah 43b:18:2.english: Know that it is due to the importance of a limb, for behold, if it were lacking a little bit - From the limb, such that it is less than a lentil-bulk, would it impart impurity?

Rashi on Niddah 43b:19:1.hebrew: עכבר דים - אינו מטמא, כדתניא בהעור והרוטב (חולין דף קכו:), דעל הארץ כתיב:
Rashi on Niddah 43b:19:1.english: A sea mouse - It does not impart impurity, as it is taught in [the chapter] Ha'or VeHaRotev (Chullin 126b), that "upon the earth" is written.

Rashi on Niddah 43b:1:1.hebrew: וירדה וטבלה - לשם יהודית. אם תמצי לומר: בזבה נעקרו מימי רגליה וירדה וטבלה, אזלינן בתר עקירה — ה"מ בישראל, דטומאתו מדאורייתא:
Rashi on Niddah 43b:1:1.english: And she descended and immersed - For the sake of [becoming] a Jewish woman. If you should say that in [the case of a] zava whose urine was uprooted and she descended and immersed, we follow the uprooting — this applies [only] to an Israelite, whose impurity is from the Torah.

Rashi on Niddah 43b:21:1.hebrew: כתנאי - נוגע אי במשהו, אי בכעדשה:
Rashi on Niddah 43b:21:1.english: Subject to [a dispute between] tanna'im - [Whether] one who touches [semen becomes impure] either in any amount or in a lentil-bulk.

Rashi on Niddah 43b:21:2.english: The verse states: "Or a man" - [The Gemara] initially assumes that we derive [it] from [the verse]: "Or a man who touches any creeping animal whereby he may become impure."

Rashi on Niddah 43b:22:1.hebrew: ושמעי' בעלמא תנאי דפליגי בכמה דוכתי בדון מינה ומינה ובדון מינה ואוקי באתרא. הילכך, הנהו תנאי על כרחך פליגי בנוגע בקרי: למ"ד דון מינה ומינה — דון ש"ז משרץ, דהא מקרא דשרץ ילפינן לה, דמה שרץ מטמא בנגיעה אף ש"ז בנגיעה; ומינה — מה שרץ בכעדשה כו':
Rashi on Niddah 43b:22:1.english: And we have heard in general [that there are] tanna'im who disagree in several places regarding 'infer from it and from it' and regarding 'infer from it and interpret [it] in its place'. Therefore, those tanna'im perforce disagree regarding one who touches semen: According to the one who says, 'Infer from it and from it': Derive semen from a creeping animal — for behold, we derive it from the verse concerning a creeping animal — that just as a creeping animal imparts impurity through contact, so too semen [imparts impurity] through contact; and from it: just as a creeping animal [imparts impurity] in a lentil-bulk, etc.

Rashi on Niddah 43b:22:2.hebrew: ואוקי באתרא - הנח ש"ז במקומה, כדאשכחן בראיה דבמשהו:
Rashi on Niddah 43b:22:2.english: And interpret [it] in its place - Leave semen in its place, as we find regarding seeing [an emission] that [it imparts impurity] in any amount.

Rashi on Niddah 43b:25:1.hebrew: דילמא מאו איש אשר תצא ממנו כו' ילפינן לה - ואפי' למ"ד דון מינה ומינה, הוה במשהו, דהא נגיעה מראיה יליף. ודכ"ע דון מינה ומינה הוה, דהכא ליכא פלוגתא דאוקי באתרא, דהא מיניה וביה יליף:
Rashi on Niddah 43b:25:1.english: Perhaps we derive it from "Or a man from whom, etc." - And even according to the one who says "infer from it and from it," it would be in any amount, for he derives touching from seeing [i.e., emitting]. And everyone [agrees that] it would be "infer from it and from it," because here there is no dispute of "interpret it in its place," since he derives it from within [the matter] itself.

Rashi on Niddah 43b:26:1.english: There are those who teach in accordance with Rav Pappa - [Deriving it] from: "Or a man who touches any creeping animal."

Rashi on Niddah 43b:28:1.hebrew: וזוקק ליבום - אם נולד יום אחד קודם מיתת אחיו. אבל נולד לאחר מיתת אחיו אינו זוקק, דכתיב (דברים כ״ה:ה׳) כי ישבו אחים יחדו:
Rashi on Niddah 43b:28:1.english: And binds to levirate marriage - If he was born one day before the death of his brother. But if he was born after the death of his brother, he does not bind [her], as it is written (Deuteronomy 25:5): "When brothers dwell together."

Rashi on Niddah 43b:28:2.hebrew: ופוטר מן היבום - אם נולד לאחר מיתת אביו וחיה שעה אחת ומת, אבל כל זמן שמעוברת אינו מתירה לינשא:
Rashi on Niddah 43b:28:2.english: And exempts from levirate marriage - If he was born after his father's death and lived for one hour and died; but as long as she is pregnant, [the fetus] does not permit her to marry.

Rashi on Niddah 43b:28:3.hebrew: ומאכיל בתרומה - בת ישראל שניסת לכהן ומת, ונולד לה בן לאחר מיתתו, אוכלת בשבילו בתרומה בו ביום שנולד, כדכתיב (ויקרא כ״ב:י״א) ויליד ביתו הם יאכלו בלחמו, ודרשינן: יאכילו את אמם. אבל הניחה מעוברת, אינה אוכלת בשבילו עד שיולד:
Rashi on Niddah 43b:28:3.english: And enables eating of terumah - An Israelite woman who was married to a priest and he died, and a son was born to her after his death, eats terumah on his account on the very day that he is born, as it is written (Leviticus 22:11): "and one born in his house, they may eat of his bread," and we expound: "They shall feed" [ya'akhilu] their mother. But if he left her pregnant, she does not eat [terumah] on his account until he is born.

Rashi on Niddah 43b:28:4.hebrew: ופוסל (את) [מן] התרומה - קס"ד, כגון בת כהן שניסת לישראל ומת, והניח בן יום אחד — פסלה מתרומת בית אביה כל ימי חייו, דכתיב (ויקרא כ״ב:י״ג) וזרע אין לה ושבה אל בית אביה, והא יש לה זרע. ובגמרא פריך: אפילו עובר נמי פוסל:
Rashi on Niddah 43b:28:4.english: And he disqualifies (the) [from] terumah - One might have thought [that this refers to a case] such as the daughter of a priest who married an Israelite, and he died and left behind a one-day-old son — he disqualifies her from the terumah of her father's house all the days of his life, as it is written (Leviticus 22:13): "And she has no child, and returns to her father's house" — and behold, she has a child. But in the Gemara it objects: Even a fetus also disqualifies [her]!

Rashi on Niddah 43b:6:1.hebrew: לח מטמא - דהחתים משמע לח, שהיבש אינו חותם פי האמה, דנפיל:
Rashi on Niddah 43b:6:1.english: Moist [discharge] imparts impurity - For "stopped up" implies moist [discharge], since dry [discharge] does not seal the opening of the penis, as it falls off.

Rashi on Niddah 43b:8:1.hebrew: רר - משמע לח, כמו (שמוא"ל א כא) ויורד רירו:
Rashi on Niddah 43b:8:1.english: Run - Means moist, as in (I Samuel 21): "And let his saliva run down."

Rashi on Niddah 43b:8:2.hebrew: בזובו חדא - זאת תהיה טומאתו בזובו - חדא, רר - תרי, את זובו - תלת, לקרבן:
Rashi on Niddah 43b:8:2.english: "In his issue" is one - "This shall be his impurity in his issue" is one; "runs" is two; "with his issue" is three, [which obligates him] to bring an offering.

Rashi on Niddah 43b:9:1.english: Or stopped up - [This teaches that only a] moist [discharge imparts impurity].

Rashi on Niddah 43b:9:2.english: From his issue, it is his impurity - [With] part of his issue, there is the impurity of zivah.

Tosafot on Niddah 43b:11:1.hebrew: עד שיצא מבשרו - ובפרק בנות כותים (לעיל נדה דף לה.) דדריש מבשרו ולא מחמת אונסו, תרתי שמעת מינה. וא"ת: ול"ל קרא עד שיצא מבשרו? מהיכא תיתי שיטמא בפנים כבחוץ? דאי מנדה וזבה — הא בריש בנות כותים (נדה דף לב:) מצריך קרא לרבות קטן לזב ולנדה ולזבה, ולא ילפינן מהדדי! וי"ל, דהוה ילפינן מנדה וזבה ופולטת במה הצד. לר"ש נמי י"ל: כיון דגלי לן קרא ששוין הן זב וזבה לענין קטנים, גם לענין פנים כבחוץ היינו משוין אותם, אי לאו מבשרו:
Tosafot on Niddah 43b:11:1.english: Until it emerges from his flesh - And [regarding the fact that] in the chapter [entitled] *Benot Kutim* (above, Niddah 35a), [the Gemara] expounds: "Out of his flesh" — and not on account of an accidental cause, you deduce two [halakhot] from it. And if you say: Why do I need a verse [to teach] "until it emerges from his flesh"? From where would it occur [to us] that he should become impure internally just as externally? For if [you suggest deriving it] from a *niddah* and a *zavah* — behold, at the beginning of *Benot Kutim* (Niddah 32b), [Scripture] requires a verse to include a minor for a *zav*, for a *niddah*, and for a *zavah*, and we do not derive them from one another! And one can say: We would have derived [it] from *niddah*, *zavah*, and a woman who discharges [semen] (*poletet*), via a common denominator argument (*mah hatzad*). According to Rabbi Shimon as well, one can say: Since Scripture revealed to us that a *zav* and a *zavah* are equal regarding minors, we would also have equated them regarding [impurity] internally just as externally, were it not for [the verse] "out of his flesh" (*mibsaro*).

Tosafot on Niddah 43b:17:1.hebrew: והתנן האברים אין להם שעור - וא"ת: וכי' לא ידע דאבר שלם דוקא קאמר? וי"ל: דפריך אמאי דמשני דשום שכבת זרע קתני, דשום שרץ נמי אשכחן כגון אברים; ומשני, דלאו היינו כל שהוא, דאי חסר ליה טהור:
Tosafot on Niddah 43b:17:1.english: And didn't we learn: The limbs have no measure - And if you say: Did [the Gemara] not know that [the mishna] speaks specifically of a whole limb? And one can say: It is objecting to that which [the Gemara] answered, that [the baraita] teaches [the general] category of semen — for in the category of creeping animal we also find [this], such as limbs. And [the Gemara] answers that this is not [considered] "any amount," for if it is lacking [a bit], it is pure.

Tosafot on Niddah 43b:21:1.hebrew: מנין לרבות נוגע בשכבת זרע ת"ל או איש - מוהבגד אשר יהיה עליו שכבת זרע לא מצי למילף, דבגד חמור מאדם, דנושא הנבלה מטמא בגדים בחבורו ולא אדם, כדאמר בפ"ק דבבא בתרא (דף ט:). וא"ת: מ"ט דריש מאו איש דשרץ, ושביק או איש דכתיב בש"ז גופיה? וי"ל, דמסתבר ליה טפי לרבות נוגע מקרא דנוגע, ולא מההיא דש"ז דמיירי ברואה. וא"ת: ול"ל יתורא דאו איש? תיפוק ליה מדאיתקש ש"ז לשרץ, דמהאי טעמא ילפינן בשרץ בגד ועור משכבת זרע בפ' במה אשה (שבת דף סד.) ובפרק כיצד הרגל (ב"ק דף כה:). וי"ל, דאי לאו או איש, הוה אמינא דלא הוקשה אלא מ"ש בפירוש, כגון נוגע דשרץ לרואה דש"ז. ומצי למימר דרב פפא, דמרבה נוגע מאו איש דשרץ, הא דאמר התם דאיתקש אהדדי היינו משום דקרא דשרץ איירי בש"ז; ומאו איש דשרץ נמי לא הוה מוקמינן לנוגע בש"ז, אי לאו דאסמכינהו בהדיא:
Tosafot on Niddah 43b:21:1.english: From where [is it derived that] one who touches semen is included? The verse states: “Or a man” - From [the verse]: “And any garment [and any skin] upon which there shall be semen” (Leviticus 15:17), he could not derive [it], for a garment is more stringent than a person, as one who carries an animal carcass defiles garments while in contact [with it] (bi-hibburo), but not a person, as [the Gemara] says in the first chapter of Bava Batra (9b). And if you say: What is the reason [the Tanna] expounds [it] from “or a man” of a creeping animal (Leviticus 22:5), and leaves aside “or a man” that is written regarding semen itself (Leviticus 22:4)? And one can answer: That it was more reasonable to him to include one who touches [semen] from a verse of touching, and not from that [verse] of semen, which deals with one who sees [i.e., emits semen]. And if you say: But why do I need the superfluity of “or a man”? Let him derive it from [the fact] that semen is juxtaposed to a creeping animal, for it is due to this reason that we derive regarding a creeping animal [that it defiles] a garment and leather from semen in the chapter “Bameh Ishah” (Shabbat 64a) and in the chapter “Keitzad HaRegel” (Bava Kamma 25b)! And one can answer: That were it not for “or a man”, I would have said that they were juxtaposed only regarding that which is explicitly written, such as [one who] touches a creeping animal to [one who] sees semen. And one can say that according to Rav Pappa, who includes one who touches [semen] from “or a man” of a creeping animal: that which [the Gemara] said there, that they are juxtaposed to each other, is because the verse of a creeping animal deals with semen; and from “or a man” of a creeping animal we also would not have applied [the derivation] to one who touches semen, were it not that [Scripture] juxtaposed them explicitly.

Tosafot on Niddah 43b:28:1.hebrew: ומטמא בנגעים - משום דבנגעים כתיב (ויקרא י״ג:כ״ט) איש או אשה, ובטומאת מת נמי כתיב (במדבר י״ט:כ׳) ואיש אשר יטמא ולא יתחטא, איצטריך קרא בהו לרבויי; אבל לענין זוקק ליבום ופוטר מן היבום ומאכיל תרומה, לא כתיב איש, ולא איצטריך קרא אלא למעוטי עובר:
Tosafot on Niddah 43b:28:1.english: And becomes impure with leprous marks - Because regarding leprous marks it is written, "A man or a woman" (Leviticus 13:29), and regarding corpse impurity it is also written, "And a man who shall be impure and shall not purify himself" (Numbers 19:20), a verse was necessary in these cases to include [a one-day-old infant]; but regarding binding [a widow] to levirate marriage, exempting [a mother] from levirate marriage, and enabling [a mother] to partake of terumah, "a man" is not written, and a verse was not necessary except to exclude a fetus.

Tosafot on Niddah 43b:8:1.hebrew: את זובו תלת - לא דריש אתין; אי נמי, אתי לדרשא אחריתי:
Tosafot on Niddah 43b:8:1.english: "With his issue" [makes] three - [The Tanna] does not expound [the particle] "et" (etin); or alternatively, [the word "et"] comes for another exposition.
